phaseDialogue.name: Clark
sentences: You must be the engineer Ronan told me about. I'm <#E09500>Clark.
I coordinate the freight routes around Ironhaven's factories and warehouses.
Ronan mentioned the work you did in Town River. Sounds like you've improved quite a few routes down there.
Things are different here. We have heavier traffic, active factories, and less room to work around.
There's a freight route nearby that needs work. Come with me and I'll show you.

phaseDialogue.name: Clark
sentences: Take a look across the passage.

dialogue.name: Clark
sentences: That's one of Ironhaven's freight yards. The warehouses are just across the channel, but the trucks have to go around several factory blocks to reach them.
That detour adds time to every delivery. <#E09500>A crossing here would give the freight crews a direct route.
You used wood in CanyonCrossing and concrete in Town River. Here in Ironhaven, we'll use steel for more demanding projects.
A <#E09500>Steel Beam supports the structure and transfers loads. It can carry both tension and compression.

dialogue.name: Clark
sentences: A <#E09500>Steel Pier adds a support beneath the bridge and carries load into its foundation.
A pier can help support a long span. Where you place it and how it connects to the bridge matter.

dialogue.name: Clark
sentences: The <#E09500>Steel Rope works as a suspension cable. It carries tension and helps hold up the deck.
A <#E09500>Suspension Bridge is worth considering for a channel this wide.

dialogue.name: Clark
sentences: A <#E09500>Suspension Bridge uses main cables supported by towers. Vertical cables called <#E09500>hangers connect the main cables to the roadway.
When a truck crosses, the hangers transfer the deck load to the main cables. Those cables mainly carry <#E09500>tension.
The towers mainly carry <#E09500>compression down to the ground, and the <#E09500>anchorages resist the cables' pull.
Keep those connections in mind. A suspension bridge can span a long distance when all its parts work together.

dialogue.name: Clark
sentences: You can review the <#E09500>Suspension Bridge lesson in your Almanac before the quiz.
When you're ready, go to the <#E09500>Quiz tab and press <#E09500>Start Quiz.

optionalDialogueSequence.quizWaitingReminder: Review the Suspension Bridge lesson in your Almanac, then press Start Quiz when you're ready.

phaseDialogue.name: Clark
sentences: Good to see you again, {PlayerName}. There's another site farther into the factory district that I'd like you to look at.
This is the factory access road. The surrounding equipment limits where we can place the crossing. Let me show you the challenge.

phaseDialogue.name: Clark
sentences: Have a look at the approach to the passage.

dialogue.name: Clark
sentences: These utilities and factory structures are still in use. Moving them would interrupt operations, so we must work around them.
That leaves the traffic lane <#E09500>closer to one side of the bridge. The factory still needs a usable connection.
A load near the center and the same load near an edge can affect a real bridge differently.
An off-center load can create <#E09500>Torsion: a twisting effect around a member's length.
For the same weight, a greater sideways distance from the center of resistance can increase the twisting moment.
Engineers consider both the downward load and that twisting effect. Here, the lesson explains torsion while your bridge test checks its load-carrying members.

dialogue.name: Clark
sentences: Review the <#E09500>Torsion lesson in your Almanac. When you're ready, open the <#E09500>Quiz tab and press <#E09500>Start Quiz.

optionalDialogueSequence.quizWaitingReminder: Review how an off-center load can create torsion, then open the Almanac Quiz tab and press Start Quiz when you're ready.

phaseDialogue.name: Clark
sentences: The factory has its direct connection now. Thanks for your help, {PlayerName}.
Mills handles the larger equipment projects farther into Ironhaven. He's the person to speak to next.
